source: Cardiff University Universities' Police Science Institute independent evaluation (Sept 2018); R (Bridges) v Chief Constable of South Wales Police [2019] EWHC 2341 (Admin) / [2020] EWCA Civ 1058; South Wales Police / Motorpoint Arena press materials; news coverage
notes: STAGING FILE — new operator/force, not yet in this dataset. South Wales Police (SWP) ran the UK's first large-scale operational trial of Automated Facial Recognition (AFR), branded 'AFR Locate' (live/real-time, equivalent to this project's LFR category) and 'AFR Identify' (after-the-fact still-image matching against custody images, closer to RFR — not staged here, Locate only). Deployed May 2017-March 2018 using two NEC algorithms in sequence: 'S17' (old, May-Oct 2017) and 'M20' (new/Beta, Nov 2017-Mar 2018). SWP's own published deployment count across the full programme (cited in press/legal commentary) is approximately 50 occasions 2017-2019; the Cardiff University evaluation report has COMPLETE outcome data for only 11 deployments/event-clusters within its June 2017-March 2018 evaluation window — this staging file covers exactly those 11, since they are the only ones with verifiable per-event statistics from a primary academic source. Earlier figure of '50 deployments' (Doughty Street Chambers / press commentary) is NOT contradicted by this file having only 11 records — it reflects a broader, less granular count that includes additional minor/unrecorded deployments outside the evaluation's complete-data window. SWP deployments outside Cardiff (Op Malachite, Swansea) are also included since they are part of the same documented programme. CRITICAL CROSS-REFERENCE: this SWP programme is the direct factual basis for R (Bridges) v Chief Constable of South Wales Police [2020] EWCA Civ 1058 — already recorded in data/legal/enforcement-actions.json as legal-001. Two of Bridges' own personal AFR-scan encounters (Queen Street Cardiff, 21 Dec 2017; Motorpoint Arena Cardiff, 27 Mar 2018) are corroborated by this evaluation report and are recorded below as swp-trial-006a (Op Fulcrum/Christmas shopping deployment window) and swp-trial-011 (Motorpoint concert season) respectively — see per-record notes for the exact cross-reference. Do NOT duplicate or alter legal-001's outcome text; this file is deployment/location data only. Geocoding: Cardiff city-centre venues geocoded individually from venue/station coordinates; Porthcawl and Swansea geocoded to town centre since exact AFR van positions are not specified in sources. lat/lon for all records in this file fall OUTSIDE this project's Greater London validator bounds (lat 51.28-51.69, lon -0.51-0.34) BY DESIGN, following the precedent set by lfr-672 (Port of Hull) — South Wales is not London, but SWP's AFR Locate programme is one of the most legally significant FRT deployments in UK history and the originating force/case for the Bridges precedent that underpins this entire project's legal framing. Expect validator lat/lon-out-of-bounds WARNINGS (not errors) on every record in this file; this is intentional, not a defect. Final IDs (lfr-NNN or a new prefix) to be assigned by Jared at merge. MERGED 2026-06-28 as swp-001..009,011..015 into data/deployments/south-wales-police-lfr.json (swp-010, the unverified Liam Gallagher concert record, deliberately excluded per this project no-speculative-records rule -- it remains in this staging file for follow-up).

deployments.location_name: Cardiff city centre, Cardiff Central train station, Cardiff Airport, Churchill Way and Callaghan Square fan zones, and Principality Stadium (4 mobile vans + 4 static camera sites)
deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate trial deployment for UEFA Champions League Final (Real Madrid v Juventus); watchlist of ~1200 'red' (wanted), 'amber' (suspected), 'purple/pink' (wanted-for-offences) and 'green' (known friendlies/intelligence-only) individuals
deployments.notes: FIRST-EVER large-scale operational AFR/LFR trial in the UK (predates all Met Police trials in this dataset, which began 2016 per lfr-669). Cardiff University Universities' Police Science Institute independent evaluation (Bethan Davies, Martin Innes, Andrew Dawson; published Sept 2018) — coordinate given is Principality Stadium/city-centre centroid; the actual deployment spanned 4 mobile vans (clearly marked 'Facial Recognition') plus 4 static cameras at Cardiff Airport, Cardiff Central station, Churchill Way and Callaghan Square fan zones, and a van fixed at Principality Stadium throughout — too dispersed for a single precise point, hence 'mobile' deployment_type and city-centre approximate centroid despite confirmed data_quality on date/event/figures. Watchlist size ~1200 (NEC S17 'old' algorithm). 2632 total matches/alerts (including 'blue'/police-officer test watchlist); only 78 (3%) confirmed true positives by operators; 1 arrest. Match threshold score (.55, NEC-recommended) was later judged too low, generating a flood of false positives — this single deployment is the most widely cited example of AFR Locate's early poor accuracy (widely reported contemporaneously, e.g. Vice, Fortune, Big Brother Watch). Cross-referenced extensively in R (Bridges) v CC South Wales Police as evidence of the technology's unreliability.

deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment at the annual Porthcawl Elvis Festival; watchlist of 472 persons of interest from the South Wales Police area
deployments.notes: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Section 4. Two mobile vans, two operators per van, same NEC S17 algorithm as Champions League. data_quality set to approximate because the report does not specify exact van positioning within Porthcawl — coordinate given is the town centre. 18 total matches; 11 (61%) confirmed true positives — a much higher accuracy than the Champions League, attributed to a raised match-score threshold (.60) and lessons learned about watchlist image quality. 1 arrest. No field observations were conducted by the evaluation team at this event; figures are from South Wales Police's own system data returns.

deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment as part of Operation Fulcrum, a recurring divisional operation targeting outstanding warrants and suspects in Cardiff city centre
deployments.notes: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Section 3. One van based in Cardiff city centre, all-day deployment, NEC S17 algorithm. Per-event match/arrest figures for this specific date are not broken out separately in the evaluation report (it is referenced as the first of a recurring 'Operation Fulcrum' series, repeated later on 22 Dec 2017 using the new M20 algorithm — see swp-trial-008). data_quality approximate: exact street/van position not given, only 'Cardiff City Centre'; coordinate approximated to Cardiff city centre/Queen Street area, the documented hub of SWP city-centre deployments.

deployments.location_name: Principality Stadium and Cardiff city centre (Anthony Joshua v Carlos Takam boxing match)
deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment for the Anthony Joshua v Carlos Takam IBF heavyweight title boxing match at Principality Stadium; watchlist of 608 persons of interest
deployments.notes: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Section 4. One van at the stadium, two vans in the city centre; old S17 algorithm handled >80% of matches, but the new M20 algorithm was trialled for the first time on a single laptop moved between sites — first head-to-head comparison of the two algorithms (M20 substantially outperformed S17, especially as daylight faded). 60 non-police matches (SWP's own figures record 51 after excluding a police officer added to a watchlist for app-testing); 5 (9%) confirmed true positives; 2 arrests, including one made promptly when an intervention team was on hand at the moment of a confirmed match. Watchlist 608 individuals.

deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment for Wales v New Zealand rugby international, Autumn Internationals series
deployments.notes: Third of 4 Autumn Internationals deployments. Notable for an equipment failure: one of SWP's 14 dedicated AFR cameras (purchased at ~GBP4,800 each) was observed 'steaming up' during this game and became inoperable — later traced to a manufacturing fault affecting all 14 units, replaced under warranty before the Six Nations. 'Frames per second' setting also lowered for this and the South Africa game to reduce processing load. Per-event outcome stats not broken out; combined 4-game total recorded once against swp-trial-005. Source: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Sections 4/Locate System Performance.

deployments.location_name: Motorpoint Arena (now Utilita Arena), Mary Ann Street, Cardiff — Kasabian concert
deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment in partnership with Motorpoint Arena targeting mobile-phone theft and pickpocketing at the Kasabian concert, drawing on a UK-wide intelligence-sharing operation ('Operation Gothic'); watchlist of 442 known mobile-phone thieves/pickpockets
deployments.notes: First of SWP's purpose-built concert-venue AFR partnership with Motorpoint Arena, publicly announced in Dec 2017 (joint SWP/Motorpoint press release) as a new approach to theft-prevention at concerts, distinct from the football/rugby/boxing crowd-policing deployments. Coordinate is the arena's postcode centroid (CF10 2EQ, Mary Ann Street) — exact in-venue camera position not given. 7 non-police matches; 3 (43%) confirmed true positives; 2 individuals ordered to leave the venue and 1 arrested for 'going equipped to steal' (found wearing a women's swimsuit used to conceal stolen phones). Notably, no mobile phones were reported stolen at this event the following day, versus 20+ at comparable previous concerts without the AFR deployment — cited by SWP as the clearest demonstrable crime-prevention outcome of the whole programme. Source: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Sections 3 (Organisational Performance) and 4 (M20 Outcomes).

deployments.location_name: Cardiff city centre (Operation Fulcrum, repeat deployment)
deployments.stated_purpose: Repeat AFR Locate deployment of Operation Fulcrum (proactive warrant/suspect operation), Cardiff city centre, using the new M20 algorithm
deployments.notes: IMPORTANT CROSS-REFERENCE: this 22 Dec 2017 Cardiff city-centre Christmas-shopping-period deployment is very likely the same deployment, or occurred within days of, the AFR scan of claimant Edward Bridges in Cardiff city centre while Christmas shopping on 21 Dec 2017 — the central personal-impact fact pattern of R (Bridges) v Chief Constable of South Wales Police [2020] EWCA Civ 1058 (legal-001 in data/legal/enforcement-actions.json). The evaluation report records 'Operation Fulcrum' deployments specifically on 22 Dec 2017 (2 arrests) and 23 Dec 2017 under the name 'Operation Malachite'/'Malecite' in Swansea, not Cardiff (see swp-trial-012) — Bridges' own 21 Dec encounter is one day earlier and not itself individually named in the evaluation report, but falls within the same week-long Christmas city-centre AFR presence. Do not treat this record as definitively THE Bridges encounter — it is the closest dated, sourced deployment to it, included for its evidentiary proximity to the legal case underpinning this entire dataset's framing. 2 arrests; alert count not given in source. Source: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Section 4 (M20 New Algorithm Outcomes).

deployments.location_name: Principality Stadium and Queen Street, Cardiff (Wales v Scotland, Six Nations)
deployments.stated_purpose: AFR Locate deployment for Wales v Scotland, Six Nations rugby; 2 mobile vans, 1 stadium van, 2 operators per van
deployments.notes: First of 3 Six Nations home-game deployments (Scotland, Italy, France — all at Principality Stadium). Notable system-performance failure recorded specifically at this game: during a dense 15-20 minute crowd surge down Queen Street as spectators exited the stadium, the AFR system stopped detecting faces entirely due to a laptop processor running at 100% utilisation (the NEC system does not support multi-threading). The combined 3-game Six Nations total (48 matches, 22 confirmed true positives [46%], 5 arrests) is recorded once against this first game to avoid duplicate-counting across all 3 fixtures — see swp-trial-014/015 notes. One of the 5 Six Nations arrests was an 'end-to-end' AFR case: a suspect identified via AFR Identify (still-image matching) from nightclub CCTV in late 2017 was later spotted and arrested via AFR Locate while walking down Queen Street in February 2018 — illustrating the two AFR modes working together, though only the Locate/real-time half is in scope for this deployment-schema file. Source: Cardiff University evaluation (Sept 2018), Sections 3 (System Performance) and 4 (M20 Outcomes).
